Range shifts between two surveys of the same gradient

Source: R/range-shift.R
range_shift_resurvey.Rd

range_shift_resurvey() compares species' ranges in a historical survey and a resurvey of the same gradient (for example the same elevational transect decades apart; Moritz et al. 2008; Freeman and Freeman 2014). For each species found in both surveys it gives the shift of the lower edge, the upper edge, the midpoint and the abundance-weighted optimum, and the change in breadth; species found in only one survey are listed as "lost" or "new".

range_shift_test() asks whether species shifted on average. Species share a gradient and survey design, but their shifts are treated as the units of replication, as in published resurveys: it gives the mean shift of each measure, a bootstrap confidence interval resampling species, and an exact two-sided sign test of whether more species moved up than down. Shifts of edges at the end of the sampled gradient are unreliable, so by default edges flagged as truncated in either survey are left out of the test of that edge.

Usage

range_shift_resurvey(
  before,
  after,
  gradient,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL
)

range_shift_test(
  x,
  nboot = 999,
  conf = 0.95,
  drop_truncated = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

before, after

Long-format data of the two surveys, with the same columns.

gradient

Column giving the position of each site on the gradient, such as elevation in metres.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

x

Result of range_shift_resurvey().

nboot

Number of bootstrap resamples of species.

conf

Confidence level.

drop_truncated

Leave out edges truncated at the ends of the sampled gradient?

seed

Optional random seed.

Value

range_shift_resurvey(): a tibble with one row per species: species, status ("both", "lost", "new"), the edges in both surveys (lower_before, lower_after, ...), the shifts (shift_lower, shift_upper, shift_midpoint, shift_optimum, change_breadth) and truncated (an edge truncated in either survey).

range_shift_test(): a tibble with one row per measure: measure, n (species), mean, lower, upper (bootstrap interval), n_up, n_down, p_sign (exact sign test).

References

Freeman, B. G. and Class Freeman, A. M. (2014). Rapid upslope shifts in New Guinean birds illustrate strong distributional responses of tropical montane species to global warming. PNAS, 111, 4490-4494.

Moritz, C. et al. (2008). Impact of a century of climate change on small-mammal communities in Yosemite National Park, USA. Science, 322, 261-264.

Examples

# Two virtual surveys: every species moves 100 m upslope
before <- png_frogs
after <- png_frogs
after$elevation <- after$elevation + 100
shifts <- range_shift_resurvey(before, after,
  gradient = elevation, abundance = abundance
)
range_shift_test(shifts, nboot = 199, seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   measure      n  mean lower upper  n_up n_down   p_sign
#>   <chr>    <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int>  <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lower       42   100   100   100    42      0 4.55e-13
#> 2 upper       53   100   100   100    53      0 2.22e-16
#> 3 midpoint    55   100   100   100    55      0 5.55e-17
#> 4 optimum     55   100   100   100    55      0 5.55e-17
